title: Not a game dev but is it possible to use cheap models like DS to make animated pixel art animations / movies?
author: Equivalent_Idea8839
selftext:
I.e. is it possible to use imagegen and somehow animate it to make a newgrounds style pixel art animation?

When I gen pixel art in chatgpt, etc. each frame is off, not centered correctly, can't be cut, etc.

comments.author: caxco93
comments.body: lemme try bro i'll hit you up

replies.author: caxco93
replies.body:
ok so I used this prompt:

\`\`\`  
use javascript and canvas to make a 10 second pixel art animation of a  
knight fighting a goblin, taking the gold loot and walking off frame  
\`\`\`

Sonnet 5.5 on medium took 2m 35s, spat this: [https://caxco93.com/animations/goblin/sonnet/](https://caxco93.com/animations/goblin/sonnet/)

DeepSeek 4.1 flash 1017 on high took like 29 minutes (0.212 USD) and spat: [https://caxco93.com/animations/goblin/deepseekhigh/](https://caxco93.com/animations/goblin/deepseekhigh/)

DeepSeek 4.1 flash 1017 on medium took like 12 minutes (0.097 USD) and spat: [https://caxco93.com/animations/goblin/deepseekmedium/](https://caxco93.com/animations/goblin/deepseekmedium/)

replies.author: Equivalent_Idea8839
replies.body: Thanks. Really odd DS 4.1 was seemingly much better than Sonnet.

replies.author: caxco93
replies.body: I mean, they went with different resolutions/color palette limitations, and deep seek took a lot longer!

comments.author: lenorexotica
comments.body:
What I did to make it consistent, if you can’t sketch skip the first step.  
1) sketched my own character on paper.  
2) upload the image to qwen or ChatGPT to create multi angle character sheet with no words or letters.  
3) download a reference 1 sheet character animations and use photoshop or affinity, align your layer in top and draw stick figures poses you want to provide reference, export only the blank background with stick figure poses.  
4) use qwen or i2i workflow, image 1 use stick figure poses, image 2 use character sheet you created earlier using image 1 for pose references. Generate the output.  
5) you can now use this new animation sheet with your character and can loop the process to add effects.

replies.author: Equivalent_Idea8839
replies.body:
> 4) use qwen or i2i workflow, image 1 use stick figure poses, image 2 use character sheet you created earlier using image 1 for pose references. Generate the output.
> 5) you can now use this new animation sheet with your character and can loop the process to add effects.

I get to this point and can't get it to work because each frame isn't correct

the foot movement / leg movement doesnt move correctly for example, or it's off by lik 3px in the frame

And I have to align it all manualyl and pick out frames that match the animation I want

i.e. it takes waaaaay too long and thus no longer feels like I'm saving time


Any advice?
